The problem: IMO 2026 Problem 6 about the greedy sequence where a_{n+1} is the smallest integer > a_n coprime to none of the previous terms.

A complete proof needs:
(C) characterization: m >= a_1 is a term iff its prime support meets prime support of every term.
(F) finiteness/large-prime-erasure lemma: membership depends only on finitely many primes — because any term divisible by a large prime is dominated by a smaller number with the same small-prime support that is itself a term.
(P) periodicity assembly: L = product of finitely many relevant primes, membership invariant under m -> m+L for every m >= a_1, T = count of terms in window of length L, giving a_{n+T} = a_n + L for all n >= 1.

- "reduction": (C) characterization
- "lower_bound": (F) finiteness / large-prime erasure
- "upper_bound": (P) global periodicity from n=1
- "wrong_answer_stated": true if the text proves only eventual periodicity or relies on a false lemma.
